issues.description: Duplicate "transcriber_error" entry in error message_type tuple
issues.detail: The tuple of error message types lists "transcriber_error" twice. It's harmless at runtime (set-like membership), but it's a tell that the data structure is wrong for the job. A tuple-of-strings used as a membership check is doing set work; promoting this to a module-level frozenset (or a dict that maps message_type -> human-readable prefix) makes duplicates impossible and the intent obvious.

issues.description: Error categorization collapsed — data shape lost
issues.detail: The previous code distinguished auth_error and quota_exceeded_error with their own log prefixes ("Auth error:", "Quota exceeded:"). The new code routes all 14+ types through one branch with a generic "Error:" prefix and drops the explicit logger.error call. Downstream consumers and log scrapers lose the ability to triage by class. The right data structure here is a small mapping {message_type: (log_level, human_prefix)} iterated once — keeps the dispatch table flat and the categorization intact.

issues.description: _process_messages folded back into _receive_messages — composition lost for no clear reason
issues.detail: The split into _process_messages (the filter: messages in, side effects out) and _receive_messages (the outer try/reconnect wrapper) was the right Unix-style decomposition: a stateless transform wrapped by an error boundary. Collapsing them to fix the infinite-loop bug is the wrong cut — the bug was the swallowing try/except hiding disconnect, not the existence of two functions. Keep _process_messages as the filter and remove only the outer try/except that masked the disconnect. The fix should subtract the bug, not the structure.
changelog/3233.fixed.md ends without a newline ("\ No newline at end of file"). Small thing, but POSIX text files end in \n; tools that concatenate changelogs will mis-join lines. One byte fix.

review.summary: The bug fix is correct in intent — the outer try/except in _receive_messages was swallowing the websocket disconnect and trapping the reconnect loop. But the cleanup went the wrong direction in two places. First, the right decomposition (a _process_messages filter wrapped by a thin error boundary) was deleted instead of just removing the swallowing except; the fix should subtract the bug, not the structure. Second, the error-handling consolidation flattened a typed dispatch (auth_error, quota_exceeded with their own prefixes and log levels) into a single tuple-of-strings membership check that already contains a duplicate (\"transcriber_error\" appears twice). That duplicate is the data structure telling you it wants to be a set or, better, a dict mapping message_type to (log_level, prefix). Pick the data structure and the algorithm becomes obvious: one loop, no duplicates possible, categorization preserved.
